More polynomial functions

Source: R/polys-extra.R
polys-extra.Rd

sym_decompose(f) (SymPy's decompose(); the name clashes with stats::decompose()) writes f as a composition g1(g2(...)) and returns the list of components. gff_list(f) is the greatest factorial factorization, a list of list(factor, k). subresultants(f, g) returns the subresultant polynomial remainder sequence. sym_trunc(f, p) reduces coefficients to symmetric residues modulo p. symmetrize(f, ...) writes a symmetric polynomial in elementary symmetric polynomials and returns list(symmetric, remainder) (with formal = TRUE also the symbols s1, s2, ... and their definitions). rational_interpolate(data, degnum, x) fits a rational function with numerator degree degnum through the points. minimal_polynomial(e, x) (alias minpoly()) is the minimal polynomial of an algebraic number built from rationals, I, radicals, sums, products and cos/sin of rational multiples of pi. swinnerton_dyer_poly(n, x) has the roots +-sqrt(2) +- ... +- sqrt(p_n). nth_power_roots_poly(f, n) has the n-th powers of the roots of f. intervals(f) isolates the real roots in rational intervals (refined to width eps, within inf and sup) by continued fractions as SymPy, refine_root(f, s, t, eps, steps) narrows one, and ground_roots(f) gives the rational roots with multiplicities. hurwitz_conditions(f, x) and schur_conditions(f, x) are the stability conditions: expressions that must all be positive. poly_from_expr(e) returns list(Poly, gens).

Usage

sym_decompose(f, x = NULL)

gff_list(f, x = NULL)

subresultants(f, g, x = NULL)

sym_trunc(f, p, x = NULL)

symmetrize(f, ..., formal = FALSE)

rational_interpolate(data, degnum, x = Symbol("x"))

minimal_polynomial(e, x = Symbol("x"))

minpoly(e, x = Symbol("x"))

swinnerton_dyer_poly(n, x = Symbol("x"))

nth_power_roots_poly(f, n, x = NULL)

ground_roots(f, x = NULL)

intervals(
  f,
  x = NULL,
  eps = NULL,
  inf = NULL,
  sup = NULL,
  fast = FALSE,
  sqf = FALSE
)

refine_root(f, s, t, eps = NULL, steps = NULL, fast = FALSE, x = NULL)

hurwitz_conditions(f, x = NULL)

schur_conditions(f, x = NULL)

poly_from_expr(e, ...)

Arguments

f, g

Polynomials.

x

The generator.

p

Modulus.

...

Generators.

formal

Return symbols for the elementary polynomials.

data

A list of c(x, y) points.

degnum

Numerator degree.

e

An algebraic number.

n

Integer.

eps

Width of the refined interval.

inf, sup

Bounds of the search interval.

fast

Use fast continued fraction steps.

sqf

Treat f as square-free and return bare intervals.

s, t

Interval endpoints.

steps

Number of refinement steps.

Value

Expressions, lists or vectors.

Examples

x <- Symbol("x"); y <- Symbol("y")
sym_decompose(x^4 + 2*x^3 - x - 1)
#> [[1]]
#> x^2 - x - 1
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> x^2 + x
#> 
subresultants(x^2 + 2*x + 1, x^2 - 1)
#> [[1]]
#> x^2 + 2*x + 1
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> x^2 - 1
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> -2*x - 2
#> 
symmetrize(x^2 + y^2)
#> [[1]]
#> -2*x*y + (x + y)^2
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> 0
#> 
minimal_polynomial(sqrt(S(2)) + sqrt(S(3)), x)
#> x^4 - 10*x^2 + 1
intervals(x^2 - 3)
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]][[1]]
#> [[1]][[1]][[1]]
#> -2
#> 
#> [[1]][[1]][[2]]
#> -1
#> 
#> 
#> [[1]][[2]]
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]][[1]]
#> [[2]][[1]][[1]]
#> 1
#> 
#> [[2]][[1]][[2]]
#> 2
#> 
#> 
#> [[2]][[2]]
#> [1] 1
#> 
#>
